purpose: Prepare interns to design, automate, deploy, secure, observe, recover, cost-control, document, and defend cloud workloads using local laboratories or Beyond-authorized accounts.
free_tier_notice: Cloud offers, credits, quotas, eligible services, regions, and billing behavior change. Students must check current official provider terms immediately before a lab. No curriculum statement overrides the provider console, contract, or Beyond authorization.
global_rules: Remain within authorized local labs and cloud account boundaries.
Configure budgets/usage alerts before provider resources; prefer local emulators when a hard spending cap or authorization is unavailable.
Use least privilege and MFA; never place secrets, state, private keys, customer data, or billing details in repositories, prompts, screenshots, or reports.
Destroy unused disposable resources daily and independently verify the post-cleanup inventory and billing/usage view.
Production changes, public exposure, security testing, paid services, account upgrades, purchases, and external communication require explicit written approval.
Document architecture, commands, evidence, cost, errors, rollback, cleanup, limitations, time, and assistance honestly.

tools: free tiers or local cloud emulators
days.objective: Create an authorized cloud-lab readiness record, cost guardrails, and cleanup checklist.
learning_outcomes: Explain Cloud Concepts and Responsible Free-Tier Use to a supervisor in clear professional language.
Use VirtualBox, Docker, GitHub to complete the authorized lab objective safely.
Produce independently verified evidence that demonstrates: Create an authorized cloud-lab readiness record, cost guardrails, and cleanup checklist.
Apply Beyond cost, security, privacy, ethics, cleanup, and documentation standards.
core_concepts: Cloud Concepts and Responsible Free-Tier Use
practical_procedure: Review Day 0 prerequisites and read the complete Day 1 objective before changing any lab resource.
Confirm written authorization, account/sandbox boundary, region, quota, budget alert, and cleanup responsibility before provisioning.
Verify only the tools required today and record versions; prefer local emulators when provider access or free-tier status is uncertain.
Create Day_001_cloud_concepts_and_responsible_free_tier_use with evidence, config or src, output, and report folders. Prevent secrets and state files from entering version control.
Complete the practical objective: Create an authorized cloud-lab readiness record, cost guardrails, and cleanup checklist.
Record commands/configuration, expected result, observed result, resource identifiers without secrets, cost/usage check, and any deviations.
Verify independently using a second command, connectivity test, configuration diff, monitoring view, clean rerun, restore test, or peer review.
Stop and remove only assigned disposable resources; verify deletion, released IPs/storage, stopped services, and current billing/usage dashboard where applicable.
Package evidence and write a professional report covering architecture, security, cost, verification, troubleshooting, limitations, and AI/tool assistance.
safety_ethics_and_beyond_lab_rules: Use only Beyond-authorized local labs, VMs, emulators, repositories, tenants, subscriptions, projects, accounts, regions, and resource groups.
Free tier does not mean unlimited or permanently free. Confirm current provider terms, eligible services, duration, region, quotas, and billing behavior before every provider lab.
Set budget and usage alerts before creating chargeable resources. Prefer a local equivalent when a hard spending cap is unavailable. Destroy unused resources daily and verify cleanup.
Never expose access keys, tokens, passwords, private keys, connection strings, customer data, public IP services, state files, or billing information in public repositories or screenshots.
Use least privilege, MFA where available, private-by-default networking, approved images/packages, encryption, logs, and human approval for consequential changes.
Do not scan, attack, stress-test, expose, purchase, upgrade, or modify production/shared resources without explicit written authorization.
Keep time, costs, failed attempts, troubleshooting, AI assistance, limitations, and cleanup records truthful.
self_check_questions: Can you explain Cloud Concepts and Responsible Free-Tier Use to a supervisor in under two minutes without reading?
What evidence proves that you completed “Create an authorized cloud-lab readiness record, cost guardrails, and cleanup checklist.” rather than only viewing a console screen?
Which shared-responsibility, IAM, network, data, availability, cost, or cleanup failure is most relevant today?
How did you independently verify the result, and can another intern reproduce it?
What would you inspect first if the demonstration failed five minutes before review?
Which resources could continue generating cost, and what evidence proves they were stopped or destroyed?
Why is the result ready—or not ready—for production, and who must approve the next action?

evidence_checklist.requirement: Privacy-reviewed baseline showing the authorized lab, active environment/profile, region or local context, and cost/usage guardrail without secrets.
Configurations, code, diagrams, tests, runbook, and outputs needed to reproduce the lab; exclude credentials, private data, caches, binary secrets, and sensitive state.
Expected versus observed result plus a second command/test, monitoring view, clean rerun, restore check, configuration diff, or peer-review note.
Resource inventory before and after cleanup, budget/usage check, deletion or stop evidence, and any item escalated to a supervisor.
Professional report with concepts, architecture, environment, procedure, result, security, cost, verification, troubleshooting, limitations, cleanup, assistance disclosure, and references.
